findings: RamcovGX.tex:1156 defines semi-local simple connectedness as 'every loop γ in X of base point x is trivial in X'; read literally this says π₁(X,x) = 1 for all x. It should read 'every loop γ in U'. The paper's own Definition at :1451 and Remark :1456 use the correct version (loops in V∩U).

RamcovGX.tex:1156: 'necessary and sufficient condition ... to admit a universal covering' — both halves are formalized (semilocallySimplyConnected_iff_exists_simplyConnected_cover) for a path-connected, locally path-connected space; Hausdorffness is never needed.

CORRECTED (round 1; the round-0 report wrongly said the paper states no composition result). The proof of prop:branched_covering_composition, direction (ii)⇒(i), RamcovGX.tex:1137, concludes '(q∘p)|X_1^{Z_1} is a composition of covering hence a covering' with no finiteness of fibres and no semilocal simple connectedness of Z_1, which is only an open portly subset of Z. The composite of two coverings is not a covering in general (classical counterexamples over a base that is not semilocally simply connected, Hawaiian-earring type); the general failure is NOT proved here. The two true forms are formalized: isCoveringMap_comp_of_finite (finite fibres of q, the paper's second map — which cannot serve :1137, branched coverings there may have infinite fibres) and isCoveringMap_comp_of_semilocallySimplyConnected (Z_1 locally path-connected and semilocally simply connected — the paper does not assume the latter of Z_1). This is a possible DEC-27 missing hypothesis in a proof another package must formalize; flagged for the prop:branched_covering_composition package. (:1123, direction (i)⇒(ii), uses 'composition of coverings' only descriptively: there q∘p is already known to be a covering on the ordinary locus, so no composition theorem is invoked.)
questions: Reading of :1156: 'loop in X' taken as 'loop in U' (Hatcher's definition, and the dispatch's). Confirm, or record that the dispatch's definition supersedes the :1156 wording (then the row is closed).

For the prop:branched_covering_composition package and the author: at :1137, which hypothesis makes (q∘p)|X_1 → Z_1 a covering — finite fibres of q, semilocal simple connectedness of Z_1 (e.g. inherited from a standing assumption of the section), or an argument specific to the ordinary loci of branched coverings? As written it invokes the composite-of-coverings theorem, which is false in general.

kb_proposals: Universal cover as a structure ⟨pt, cls : Path.Homotopic.Quotient y₀ pt⟩ with topology generateFrom of basic sets B(c,U); B(c',U) = B(c,U) whenever c' ∈ B(c,U), so the basis axiom needs no local path-connectedness.

Canonical lift t ↦ c·[δ ∘ segPath 0 t] with segPath the affine path in I; I is SimplyConnectedSpace via (convex_Icc 0 1).contractibleSpace, which makes every reparametrisation identity a one-liner (paths_homotopic). Endpoint equalities of the dependent pairs go through Path.Homotopic.hpath_hext (namespace Path.Homotopic, not .Quotient) and cast_heq.

To prove IsCoveringMap, use IsOpen.trivializationDiscrete via GX.isEvenlyCovered_of_sheets (open sheets, InjOn, SurjOn, pairwise disjoint, cover; f continuous and open); GX.IsEvenlyCovered.exists_sheets goes the other way.
grind on Path.Homotopic.Quotient group-like identities timed out (whnf) here; explicit trans_assoc/symm_trans/trans_refl calc is instant.
FundamentalGroup is End, so a * b = b ≫ a = b.trans a; the action c ↦ (g⁻¹)·c is then a homomorphism by mul_inv_rev, with no symm lemma needed.

Generalized field notation finds GX.Foo.bar for h : Foo only after `open GX` (it works in a downstream file with `open GX in`, but NOT inside `namespace GX` itself): inside the defining file call GX.IsPreconnected.subset_of_pairwise_disjoint explicitly.

Composite of coverings over an LPC SLSC base: sheets = path components of (p∘q)⁻¹W for a good path-connected W; injectivity from IsCoveringMap.homotopicRel_iff_comp applied twice (p then q) to the loop's null-homotopy; LPC of E from IsLocalHomeomorph via OpenPartialHomeomorph + JoinedIn.map_continuousOn.
